summary: Latency regression (p95/p99 spikes) tied to continuous batching; intermittent 504/timeouts
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-02-20 08:30 UTC we observed a regression in tail latency for customer Acme Finance. P95 and P99 for text-generation requests increased from baseline ~200-350ms to spikes of 2-6s, and several requests resulted in 504 gateway timeouts. Impact: customer-facing app experiences degraded UX; several production requests timed out and triggered client-side retries, increasing load. Environment: Production (dedicated pool for Acme Finance) in us-east-1. Observed across multiple model variants pinned by the customer (open-llama-7b-v2). Observed behavior: sudden p95/p99 spikes correlating with large continuous-batching windows; sustained higher queueing times when GC/eviction cycles or kernel scheduling coincide with batch flush thresholds. Expected behavior: stable p95/p99 within historical baselines (~200-350ms) and no elevated 504s.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Send sustained mix of short and long completion requests (avg tokens/request ~150) to customer's dedicated endpoint at 100 rps.
2. Observe tail latencies in the Redwood Console per-route dashboard for the endpoint over 10-30 minutes.
3. Correlate with serving-runtime continuous-batching metrics (batch_size_distribution, batch_wait_ms, batch_flush_events) and scheduler logs.
4. Reproduce in staging by running synthetic load with matching token distribution and enabling continuous batching config used in prod.
logs: 2026-02-20T08:32:14Z ERROR gateway 504 Gateway Timeout - request_id=req_8f3b2c - endpoint=acme-prod - duration=6002ms
2026-02-20T08:33:02Z WARN serving-runtime batch_wait_ms=1820 batch_size=32 max_batch_latency=2000 eviction_cycle_ms=1200
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: continuous batching policy (max_wait_ms + adaptive flush) is allowing requests to sit in queue longer under mixed short+long token workloads, causing p95/p99 spikes.
Observed correlation between batch_wait_ms increases and p99 spikes in console. Spikes coincide with kernel switch events and eviction cycles.
Reproduced in staging when running synthetic load with identical request size distribution. Disabling continuous batching in staging removed p99 spikes.

Related tickets: SUP-41278 and SUP-42199 reported similar symptoms last quarter tied to batch kernel scheduling; that investigation led to a kernel prioritization patch (PR #987) which has not yet been rolled to all regions.

Potential contributing factors: mixed request lengths, GPU kernel selection path that temporarily increases per-token exec time, and continuous-batching adaptive flush thresholds that are too permissive for this workload mix.
Data collected: per-request trace samples, batch composition snapshots, scheduler traces, and kernel latency histograms. Full traces uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/traces/SUP-43121/
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporarily disabled continuous batching on Acme's dedicated pool at 2026-02-20T10:15Z which reduced p95/p99 to baseline. Ongoing: preparing a targeted fix that adjusts adaptive flush thresholds and ensures kernel switching is non-blocking (patch in review: PR #987). Next steps: roll patch to canary cluster, monitor 24h, then schedule production rollout during low-traffic window. Customer notified and monitoring agreement in place.
